question: What is the primary goal of healthcare waste management systems?

options.A: To reduce the financial operating costs of large tertiary medical centres
options.B: To safely handle waste from generation to final disposal without causing harm
options.C: To recycle all single-use plastics used within surgical theatre suites
options.D: To completely eliminate the generation of any biological matter in hospitals

explanation: Management systems exist primarily to protect public health and the environment by safely controlling every phase of waste handling. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h1)

question: Which factor most severely compromises safe healthcare waste management in many Nigerian secondary health facilities?

options.A: A total absence of any biomedical materials used in patient care
options.B: Strict enforcement of federal environmental protection penalties
options.C: Inadequate funding and unreliable infrastructure like power supply
options.D: An excess of highly trained environmental sanitation officers

explanation: Basic operational failures such as broken incinerators and lack of funding remain major barriers to effective waste processing across local facilities. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h1)

question: Which item falls directly under the classification of pathological waste?

options.A: An expired bottle of oral paracetamol suspension
options.B: A used plastic syringe barrel without the needle
options.C: An empty cardboard box used for medical supplies
options.D: A surgically removed gallbladder or body tissue

explanation: Pathological waste specifically comprises human tissues, organs, and body parts generated during medical procedures. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h2)

question: Why must pharmaceutical and chemical waste be categorized separately from general municipal trash?

options.A: Because pharmaceutical drugs lose their chemical stability inside standard landfills
options.B: Because chemical containers are always made of heavy industrial steel alloys
options.C: Because they can be easily crushed and recycled into children's plastic toys
options.D: Because they can contaminate water sources and toxic compounds can enter the food chain

explanation: Hazardous chemicals and drugs leach into soil and groundwater, posing severe long-term environmental and toxicological threats. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h2)

question: A hospital procurement officer practices waste minimization by taking which action?

options.A: Purchasing medical supplies that feature excessive layers of non-recyclable cardboard packaging
options.B: Ordering double the normal quantity of single-use plastic syringes to secure bulk discounts
options.C: Disposing of all hospital records immediately after a patient is discharged from the ward
options.D: Selecting reusable surgical instruments that can withstand frequent steam sterilization

explanation: Choosing durable, reusable alternatives directly reduces the sheer volume of single-use disposable items entering the waste stream. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h3)

question: What inventory management method helps prevent large quantities of pharmaceuticals from expiring in hospital stores?
explanation: The First-In, First-Out approach ensures older stock gets used before newer shipments arrive, preventing expiration waste. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h3)

question: At what point in the clinical workflow must healthcare waste segregation occur?

options.A: Inside the municipal waste truck during transit to the landfill
options.B: By environmental sanitation workers at the final dumpsite
options.C: Only when the central incinerator is undergoing routine maintenance
options.D: Directly at the point of origin where the waste is generated

explanation: Segregation must happen immediately at the bedside or treatment room to prevent hazardous items from mixing with general refuse. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h4)

question: A nurse finishes administering an intramuscular injection in a busy immunization clinic. What is the safest immediate action regarding the needle?

options.A: Bend the needle with forceps and throw it onto the procedure tray
options.B: Throw the syringe with the uncovered needle into the black general waste bin
options.C: Drop the uncovered needle directly into the puncture-proof safety box
options.D: Recap the needle carefully using two hands and place it in the pocket

explanation: Sharps must be discarded immediately without recapping into a puncture-resistant container to prevent accidental inoculation injuries. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h4)

question: At what capacity should a yellow infectious waste bag be securely closed and removed from the ward?

options.A: Only at the exact end of every calendar month
options.B: When the local municipal authority vehicle arrives at the gate
options.C: When it reaches approximately three-quarters (75%) full capacity
options.D: When it is completely stuffed and overflowing to save on bags

explanation: Bags are sealed at three-quarters capacity to ensure they can be safely tied off without tearing or spilling contents. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h5)

question: Why is compressing a filled infectious waste bag down with bare or gloved hands strictly prohibited?

options.A: It stretches the plastic bag and ruins its aesthetic appearance
options.B: It slows down the speed of the ward cleaning routine significantly
options.C: It creates a high risk of puncture injuries from improperly segregated sharps
options.D: It releases unpleasant odours that disturb patients resting nearby

explanation: Pressing down on waste bags drives hidden needles through the plastic, causing severe needlestick injuries and potential pathogen exposure. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h5)

question: What is the maximum recommended on-site storage duration for infectious waste in warm tropical climates?
explanation: Warm ambient temperatures accelerate biological decay and vector attraction, necessitating prompt removal within 48 hours. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h6)

question: Which structural feature is essential for a hospital's temporary waste storage room?

options.A: Washable hard surfaces, proper drainage, and pest control
options.B: Direct architectural connection to the hospital cafeteria
options.C: Carpeted flooring to absorb liquid spills quietly
options.D: Large glass windows allowing direct sunlight exposure all day

explanation: Storage areas must be easy to wash and disinfect while preventing vector infestation due to the hazardous nature of the contents. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h6)

question: What mechanism does an autoclave use to render infectious healthcare waste safe?

options.A: Open-air burning in a shallow brick pit

explanation: Autoclaves use high-temperature pressurized steam to destroy pathogenic microorganisms effectively. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h7)

question: What is a major environmental drawback of operating a poorly maintained low-temperature incinerator?

options.A: It turns all hazardous waste into harmless drinking water
options.B: It completely freezes the surrounding soil layers
options.C: It emits toxic pollutants like dioxins and furans into the air
options.D: It increases the local municipal electricity supply voltage

explanation: Incomplete combustion at low temperatures releases hazardous airborne chemical pollutants that harm public health. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h7)

question: Which specific vaccination is essential for healthcare workers handling medical waste due to bloodborne exposure risks?
explanation: Hepatitis B vaccination protects workers against potential transmission following accidental sharps injuries or fluid splashes. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h8)

question: What is the primary purpose of maintaining an accident and injury register in a healthcare facility?

options.A: To penalize staff members who make administrative paperwork errors
options.B: To track workplace incidents, monitor risks, and improve safety protocols
options.C: To calculate the annual bonus for senior hospital management staff
options.D: To provide entertainment reading for incoming clinical students

explanation: Tracking incidents helps identify recurring hazards and ensures injured staff receive timely post-exposure evaluation and care. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h8)
